title: Enhancement of spin current in Fe$_{85}$Co$_{15}$/Ni$_{80}$Fe$_{20}$ bilayers via interlayer ferromagnetic coupling
authors: A. A. Pérez Martínez, D. Velázquez Rodríguez, D. Goijman, T. Torres, M. H. Aguirre, J. Gómez, A. Butera, E. De Biasi, J. Milano
abstract: We present a detailed study on how the strength of the interlayer magnetic coupling on Fe$_{85}$Co$_{15}$/Ni$_{80}$Fe$_{20}$ bilayers modifies the spin wave behavior of this system. A series of Fe$_{85}$Co$_{15}$/Ni$_{80}$Fe$_{20}$ bilayers deposited on MgO[100] substrates were grown by magnetron sputtering. Magnetic characterization of the samples was performed using a vibrating sample magnetometer and magneto-optical Kerr effect. The in-plane hysteresis loops reveal a cubic magnetic anisotropy of magnetocrystalline origin, with easy and hard axis along the [100] and [110] Fe-Co crystallographic directions, respectively. Ferromagnetic resonance measurements were performed to analyze the in-plane angular dependence of the resonance field, and also the resonance field at several frequencies was determined along the hard axis. By using a bilayer model in the frame of the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert magnetization equation of motion, the magnetization precession components were calculated, as well as the dependence of precession area on the Fe-Co layer thickness and the ferromagnetic interlayer coupling. We observe a maximum in the area of the ellipsoid generated by the magnetization precession of the permalloy layer at a certain exchange constant, showing that this effect could be used to maximize the injected spin currents, which could be tuned by changing the interlayer exchange constant in bilayer systems, the saturation magnetization of the materials, or the excitation frequency.
summary: This work systematically studies spin current enhancement in ferromagnetic bilayers by modeling the influence of interlayer exchange coupling ($J_{ex}$). Using a combination of VSM, MOKE, and broadband FMR measurements alongside theoretical LLG simulations, the authors demonstrate that maximizing spin current requires tuning $J_{ex}$ to an intermediate value. This provides a pathway for designing spintronic devices with optimized spin injection efficiency.
main_problem: The study investigates how tuning the strength of interlayer magnetic coupling influences spin wave behavior and maximizes injected spin currents in $	ext{Fe}_{85}	ext{Co}_{15}/	ext{Ni}_{80}	ext{Fe}_{20}$ ferromagnetic bilayers.
main_result: A maximum in the magnetization precession area, indicative of enhanced spin current injection, is observed when the interlayer exchange coupling constant ($J_{ex}$) is tuned to an intermediate value. This effect can be optimized by controlling $J_{ex}$, material saturation magnetizations ($	ext{M}_s$), or excitation frequency.
method: The research combines experimental characterization (VSM, MOKE, FMR using VNA) with theoretical modeling based on the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation of motion and a derived free energy functional.
model_or_system: The system is an epitaxial $	ext{Fe}_{85}	ext{Co}_{15}/	ext{Ni}_{80}	ext{Fe}_{20}$ bilayer grown on MgO[100] substrates. The dynamics are modeled using a bilayer Hamiltonian incorporating Zeeman, shape, cubic/uniaxial anisotropy, and the interlayer exchange coupling term ($J_{ex}$).
key_observables: Magnetization precession area (diagnostic for spin current), resonance field ($	ext{H}_r$), saturation magnetization ($	ext{M}_s$), and the interlayer exchange constant ($J_{ex}$).
important_parameters:
Interlayer coupling strength ($J_{ex}$), material thicknesses, excitation frequency ($
u \sim 9.7-35	ext{ GHz}$), and $	ext{M}_s$ of constituent layers.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a bilayer model within the LLG equation framework, linearizing dynamics for small oscillations to analyze coupled acoustic and optical modes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate magnetization hysteresis loops showing anisotropy axes; FMR spectra show mode splitting related to $J_{ex}$; and key figures plot the precession area versus $J_{ex}$ or $	ext{M}_s$, demonstrating the maximum enhancement point.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by characterizing the magnetic properties (anisotropy, $	ext{M}_s$) of the bilayers experimentally. It then develops a theoretical model using the free energy and LLG equation to predict coupled spin dynamics. Finally, it analyzes how tuning $J_{ex}$ leads to an optimal condition for maximizing the precession area, which correlates with maximum spin current.
why_interesting: While focused on spintronics, the detailed analysis of coupled magnetic excitations (acoustic/optical modes) and the use of nonlinear dynamic equations ($	ext{LLG}$) provide rich mathematical structures relevant to open quantum systems dynamics and energy dissipation in nanoscale magnetic circuits.
